name: Marching for Freedom: Rights Struggles Around the World
description: From the slaves of Haiti to the pass-law protesters of South Africa, how ordinary people fought for equal rights, the vote and a voice in many countries.

checkpoints.name: Against bondage
checkpoints.note: The Haitian Revolution of Toussaint Louverture shows that enslaved people can free themselves. Wollstonecraft claims rights for women, Wilberforce and others bring about Britain's end of slavery, and Douglass, Tubman and Sojourner Truth help bring Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation.

checkpoints.name: Votes and nonviolence
checkpoints.note: Susan B. Anthony and Emmeline Pankhurst fight for women's votes, and American women win the vote with the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920. In India, Gandhi's Salt March turns nonviolent resistance into a mass movement.

checkpoints.name: Rights for all
checkpoints.note: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights sets a world standard. In America, Brown v. Board, the bus boycott sparked by Rosa Parks and led by King, and the wider movement win the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, and Malcolm X and the Panthers push further. Sharpeville shows apartheid's violence, and Stonewall opens a new fight.

checkpoints.name: People power
checkpoints.note: Soweto's children and Steve Biko challenge apartheid, while in Poland Walesa and Solidarity shake Communism and in Czechoslovakia Havel leads the Velvet Revolution. Protesters fill Tiananmen Square.

checkpoints.name: After the walls
checkpoints.note: Nelson Mandela walks free and wins South Africa's 1994 election. Aung San Suu Kyi in Myanmar and Malala Yousafzai for girls' education show that the struggle continues, and the Arab Spring of 2011 shows protest spreading by phone and screen.
